The main takeaway from our work is that

the final stages of deformation of an accreted wedge, as recorded in the Ligurian units, are characterized by shortening events, which are unrelated to the main thrusting phases that affected the wedge during its early stages of deformation.

the Ligurian units, which were previously thought to have undergone a simple, continuous, and uniform tectonic evolution from their final subduction to their final emplacement onto a foreland margin, were in fact subjected to several deformation phases, each characterized by a specific kinematic pattern.

, at least in the case study presented here, the tectonics of the accreted wedge is largely independent of the tectonothermal history of the foreland, as well as of the backarc extensional regime that developed after the accretion of the accretory complex.
